operator_visible_outcome: A named native Linux AMD64 host is classified feasible or unavailable while Production execution remains unsupported

inputs.validation: Bounded canonical host, kernel, boot, cgroup v2, filesystem, namespace, fixture and probe identities

outputs.validation: Canonical primitive, process-accounting and hostile-fixture outcomes bound to exact Product, probe and fixture identities

canonical_state: A feasibility observation is non-authoritative platform evidence
Windows AMD64 remains the only qualified operation boundary
Root-relative resolution beneath the owned temporary root refuses symbolic links, magic links, parent escapes and absolute-path escapes
A fixture uses private PID, IPC, UTS, mount and network namespaces, a private proc mount, disabled loopback and only descriptors 0, 1 and 2
A fixture is copied into a sealed non-writable descriptor then validated as an x86-64 static ELF executable with no PT_INTERP and bound by SHA-256, device and inode

A feasible observation records exact Product and probe commits, probe and fixture SHA-256 values, Linux architecture, kernel release, boot ID, cgroup mount and subtree identities, filesystem type and device, namespace configuration and primitive outcomes
derived_state: Primitive availability and first refusal reason

authorities.grant: Create only bounded temporary cgroups, explicitly mapped namespaces, files and hostile fixture processes beneath declared local roots
authorities.refusal: Reject missing delegation, isolation, cleanup, durability or observation identity

trust_boundaries.treatment: Query bounded primitives and challenge them with hostile fixtures
Bind exact identities without treating feasibility as operation qualification

resources.acquisition: Use clone3(CLONE_INTO_CGROUP) to create the namespace bootstrap atomically in the delegated cgroup before execution
resources.bound: At most 16 kernel tasks for the trusted gated Go bootstrap then four hostile-fixture tasks: fixture, one deliberate descendant, one challenge helper and one remaining owned slot; the process challenge lowers the fixture limit to one; hostile memory is limited to 67108864 bytes with memory.swap.max set to zero; 2000 milliseconds per fixture
resources.release: Kill and join the complete owned cgroup tree after recording every member PID and role
resources.cleanup_failure: Record failure and do not claim feasibility
resources.cancellation: Kill the owned cgroup tree when the probe context ends
resources.join: Observe cgroup emptiness and every owned process exit before returning; missing accounting fails the observation

resources.acquisition: Create one bounded same-directory temporary record beneath the named local ext4 or XFS evidence root
resources.release: Fsync the temporary file, publish with renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE), fsync the parent directory, inspect then remove only the owned fixture tree
resources.cleanup_failure: Record failure and retain no feasibility claim
resources.recovery: Discard incomplete probe output and regenerate after owned-resource cleanup

platforms.refusal: Production execution remains unavailable during feasibility

invariants.statement: No fixture process executes before clone3(CLONE_INTO_CGROUP) places its bootstrap in the owned cgroup; the fixture has private PID, IPC, UTS, mount and network namespaces, a private proc mount, disabled loopback, only descriptors 0, 1 and 2, sealed non-writable static x86-64 ELF identity with no PT_INTERP and root-relative resolution refuses links and path escapes
invariants.falsifier: A fixture begins outside the owned cgroup, user mapping, mount, /proc or loopback state differs from the observation or it gains network, host-file or ambient descriptor access
invariants.residual_uncertainty: Feasibility does not qualify the complete operation

invariants.statement: Native persistence qualification cannot enable Linux operation constructors
invariants.falsifier: A Linux caller constructs the supervisor or operation, or persistence qualification is treated as execution authority
invariants.residual_uncertainty: A later enablement slice must replace this refusal coherently

invariants.statement: Feasibility requires canonical named native host, cgroup, namespace, fixture, probe and filesystem evidence
invariants.falsifier: Cross-compiled, emulated, skipped, incomplete or identity-unbound evidence is accepted
invariants.residual_uncertainty: One host cannot establish other-kernel or filesystem support

invariants.statement: A feasible observation proves same-directory file fsync, renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) and parent-directory fsync on the named local ext4 or XFS filesystem
invariants.falsifier: A missing, unsupported or failed durability primitive still produces feasible
invariants.residual_uncertainty: This checks declared primitives rather than all filesystem crash semantics

success_semantics: Feasible means every declared primitive, canonical identity and hostile fixture passed on the named native host while the Production operation remained unavailable
refusal_semantics: Unavailable identifies the first missing authority or primitive, including clone3(CLONE_INTO_CGROUP), namespace mapping, descriptor allowlist, static fixture identity, process accounting or publication primitive, before worker execution
failure_semantics: Probe, fixture, cleanup or observation failure cannot produce a feasible result
cancellation_semantics: Cancellation terminates and joins every probe-owned process and retains no success claim
indeterminate_semantics: Missing, contradictory or unbound host evidence cannot produce a feasibility claim
recovery_semantics: Partial probe output is non-canonical and is regenerated after complete owned-resource cleanup
compatibility_or_reset_policy: Unused pre-release feasibility formats are replaced coherently with no compatibility reader
falsifiers: A fixture executes before clone3(CLONE_INTO_CGROUP) placement
User mapping, mount propagation, /proc or network-loopback state differs from the observation
A network, host-file or descriptor escape succeeds
A descendant survives owned-tree cleanup or process accounting exceeds four
Filesystem durability is inferred without file fsync, renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) and parent-directory fsync evidence
Linux operation becomes constructible or persistence is reported qualified without native evidence
residual_limitations: Feasibility and persistence qualification are not Linux operation support
One host does not qualify other kernels or filesystems
Seccomp, Landlock, SELinux, AppArmor and other LSM controls are not qualified
non_goals: Add a dependency, container, daemon, pool or persistent worker
deletion_criteria: Delete only when a reviewed Linux AMD64 vertical-slice contract supersedes every probe, fixture, observation and reader
